guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): the sim refuses to OFFER the DIG option when the grab bag is empty; C# always offers it and grants RelicFactory.FallbackRelic instead
guards.issue: G2 DUP: MECHANISM: Shovel.TryModifyRestSiteOptions adds `new DigRestSiteOption(player)` unconditionally (Shovel.cs:24) and DigRestSiteOption overrides nothing that could disable it -- RestSiteOption.IsEnabled is the base `=> true` (RestSiteOption.cs:37). If the bag has nothing left, PullFromFront returns null and RelicFactory substitutes FallbackRelic (RelicFactory.cs:47), so the player still gets A relic. shovel.py:24-25 returns early on `not run.has_available_relics()`, so the option does not appear at all. Still DORMANT, RECONFIRMED 2026-08-04 (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b14.py shovel`): bag has 122 relics -> options=['DIG']; bag EMPTY -> options=[] (C# still offers DIG and grants RelicFactory.FallbackRelic). Quantified: the bag holds 122 relics at run start and a DIG consumes exactly one (122 -> 121), so emptying it needs ~122 relic acquisitions in a run that offers on the order of 15-20. STALE-SWEEP CORRECTION: the prior text's secondary claim ('the sim falls back to relic_grab_bag.pop(0) regardless of rarity, run.py:595') is no longer true -- run.py's pull_relic_from_front/pull_relic_from_back (run.py:970-1078) now climb the same Shop->Common->Uncommon->Rare escalation ladder as RelicGrabBag.GetAvailableDeque (RelicGrabBag.cs:227-237) before falling back to FallbackRelic; that shared-machinery divergence has been closed since this record was written and is removed from this rationale. Porting a relic sink that drains the bag -- or a run length that does -- is what would make THIS guard (the missing DIG option / no fallback relic on an empty bag) live. Rule 7: RestSiteOption.cs, DigRestSiteOption.cs, RelicFactory.cs, RelicGrabBag.cs and run.py are not hashed here.

Checked against PROMPT.md bug class 16's named-stream trap, and this one is wired: shovel.py:27 calls run.obtain_relic_from_grab_bag() with no rarity_rng, and pull_relic_from_front's documented default is `self.rewards_rng` -- the per-player Rewards stream under a parity rng_set and the legacy shared RNG otherwise (run.py:970-1021). obtain_relic_from_grab_bag pulls and then calls run.add_relic (run.py:957-964), which is the sim's RelicCmd.Obtain -- it fires after_obtained, so a dug Sand Castle or Signet Ring applies its pickup effect exactly as a chest-granted one would. The SharedRelicGrabBag.Remove line is the multiplayer second bag keeping in sync with the per-player one; the sim has a single bag, so the removal has no counterpart to need. Rule 7: run.py is not hashed here.
